change: The existing MIX Delivery worker now retains claim, personal-archive, route-transfer and settlement knowledge through private consuming owners, including cancellation and panic cuts.
behavior: A claim distinguishes an authorized empty read from entry and success of the existing mutating claim statement. Only the exact returned immutable row storage can issue attempts; copied values or public identifiers cannot substitute another invocation.
Each attempt retains its actual delivery and lease identifiers, claimed payload and route-wake generation. Existing archive=false and optional authoritative-ID rows remain valid.

Personal-archive Stored and authenticated Replay retain their actual COMMIT receipts and returned IDs, including Replay’s original archive ID. A matching return permits routing; contradictory successful returns retain the evidence and block new permissions. Ordinary backend errors keep the existing retry policy.

Local queue acceptance remains an uncertain handoff prefix. SocketFenced, SmPersisted and BoshPersisted results consume the old worker’s settlement permission immediately. The existing pending-handoff disconnect behavior remains in force.
The cluster adapter records the actual acknowledged typed handoff before returning. A delivered boolean, unacknowledged result or error cannot grant transfer.

Renewal remains concurrent with routing only. After the existing helper has destroyed its children, a consuming scope-closed token permits settlement. Dropped pending renewal keeps its recorded facts; renewal false or failure authorizes no new settlement.
The actual route result selects one lazy ACK, defer, retry or dead-letter request. The request binds the exact source, route-wake generation and command; transfer grants no old-worker settlement.

ACK false and retry LeaseLost retain the actual no-exact-token-match COMMIT result, without inferring row absence or a new owner. Dead-letter false means NotMoved. Renewal and defer record successful autocommit statement outcomes, including false, separately from explicit COMMIT receipts.

Claim and attempt holders destroy children before owner retirement. A separate retirement guard retains cancellation, timeout and panic outcomes, including an externally caught poll panic or a child-destructor panic. Drop performs no database compensation, re-admission or retry.
compatibility: The existing SQL text, predicates, locks, active-lease checks and exact-token settlement rules remain intact. Retry still chooses from the locked persisted attempt count and route-wake generation.
Fair shared database admission, local wake conditions, route-only renewal, Delivery/PAM lane separation, stop/drain behavior, deadlines and retry policy remain unchanged.
Legacy returned-only entry points remain available. No new dependency, migration, general executor or scenario language is introduced.

validation.status: Accepted within the finite ordinary source/component scope after independent review.

new_control_scope.pure_core: 16 finite transition controls for claim knowledge/private identity, optional archive shape, Stored/Replay permission, contradictory returns, typed transfer, renewal, exclusive settlement and actual-result correspondence.
new_control_scope.runtime_and_protocol: 10 finite controls for the production holders, actual in-memory local queue/oneshot handoff, cancellation/destruction, supplied cluster receipt classification, fake statement/COMMIT cuts and the existing renewal helper.

validation.reused_control_scope: 27 unchanged controls: 25 protocol controls for legacy lazy settlement, local handoff, route classification, claim/renewal progress, cancellation/deadlines and Delivery/PAM drain/concurrency; two in-memory service controls for retained wakes and the clone-shared FIFO admission gate.
validation.format_compile_clippy_and_source_gates: Passed, including Clippy with warnings denied and the migration/source checker.

engineering_corrections: The migration/source checker’s stale producer count is corrected from 18 to 19, counting both existing compatibility and observed foreground store entries. Their fair admission requirements remain intact.

Two existing negative probes now target the actual worker ACK request boundary and the original BOSH source-extraction function. Their exactly-one mutation assertions and production verifiers remain unchanged.
The retained service compatibility DTO has a documented, struct-local dead-code expectation only outside test builds. Its fields, derives and API remain unchanged.

Earlier stopped or incomplete validation attempts remain excluded from acceptance. A fresh cold build reached its fixed time limit; the separately reviewed continuation reused only its settled isolated cache and completed under the unchanged limits.
limits: The controls exercise local ownership and finite supplied outcomes. They do not execute a complete protocol-to-service-to-PostgreSQL delivery.
Local handoff controls use the real in-memory queue and oneshot waiter, with supplied typed transport completions. They do not perform a socket write or SM/BOSH database transfer.
Cluster controls classify supplied receipts; they do not invoke a remote peer or prove cluster delivery.

Actual SQL statement/COMMIT placement and exact-source predicates are source/gate correspondence claims. Fake completion tests do not establish PostgreSQL transaction, lock, lease-clock or failure behavior.

The renewal control exercises the existing concurrent helper and pending-child destruction. Existing deadline/cancellation controls provide their own bounded evidence; they are not full observed end-to-end recovery tests.

This component does not complete full auth correlation, saved cross-domain composition, real-adapter qualification or Stage4. Historical accepted results retain their original scope; the earlier TLS response-EOF issue remains unresolved.
detailed_evidence: Detailed source snapshots, retained stops and execution records are held separately. This summary contains no raw execution metadata.
